title: Driver Services Agreement Terms: Changing Service Level and Changing Vehicle
content:
These terms of the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product apply when a Wayfare agreement moves between service levels or the driver registers a different vehicle. The active-days figure and the inspection requirement are in the level-change schedule.

**Term 1. Upgrade wait.** A move to a higher level requires the agreement to have been active long enough. The upgrade wait is counted in calendar days from the activated date: day 1 is the calendar day after activation, and the move may be made from the day after the last day of the wait. The last day of the wait itself is too early.

**Term 2. Requirements of the new level.** The move also requires the new level's entry gate, vehicle requirements and documents, and an inspection valid on the change date.

**Term 3. Vehicle no longer meeting the level.** When the registered vehicle stops meeting the level (age on the January 1 age step-up date, seats, or powertrain after a vehicle change), the agreement moves to the highest level the vehicle and the driver's rating still meet, and is never deactivated for that alone.

**Term 4. Whose request.** Changing vehicle or level is the driver's own request; a fallback move under the rating standard needs no request.

## Upgrade wait boundary (hypothetical, a 30-day wait)

| Activated date | Day 1 | Last day of the wait | Move on 2026-01-31 | Move on 2026-02-01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-01-01 | 2026-01-02 | 2026-01-31 | too early | permitted (other requirements met) |

## Hypothetical vehicle case

A Wayfare Comfort agreement with a 4-seat gasoline vehicle that reaches 7 years on January 1 no longer meets the Comfort 6-year limit. Wayfare Green does not accept gasoline, Wayfare XL needs 6 seats and the Black levels allow 6 years, so with a rating of at least 4.60 the highest level still met is Wayfare Standard (limit 15 years); the agreement moves there and is not deactivated for the vehicle's age alone.
